title: Asynchronous Pipeline (pipeAsync) with Error Recovery
concept: Point-Free Async Function Composition & Pipe Architecture
problemStatement: Implement `pipeAsync(...fns)` that chains functions from left to right, where each function can be synchronous or return a Promise. If any step throws or rejects, allow an optional recovery handler passed via `pipeAsync.recoverWith(handler)`.
interviewTrap: Using synchronous `Array.prototype.reduce` without awaiting promises inside the accumulator will return unresolved promise chains.

testCases.name: Pipes value through synchronous and async transforms in order
testCases.testFn: const add5 = x => x + 5; const doubleAsync = async x => x * 2; const sub2 = x => x - 2; const pipeline = pipeAsync(add5, doubleAsync, sub2); return pipeline(10);

testCases.name: Handles single function pipeline
testCases.testFn: const p = pipeAsync(async s => s.toUpperCase()); return p('hello');

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Currying converts a function taking N arguments `f(a, b, c)` into a sequence of N unary functions `f(a)(b)(c)`. When total collected arguments `>= fn.length`, the underlying function executes.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Point-Free Async Function Composition & Pipe Architecture.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Point-Free Async Function Composition & Pipe Architecture is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Using synchronous `Array.prototype.reduce` without awaiting promises inside the accumulator will return unresolved promise chains.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does pipeAsync handle error recovery in a point-free asynchronous pipeline?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In `pipeAsync(...fns)`, the pipeline folds functions via `fns.reduce((accPromise, fn) => accPromise.then(val => fn(val)).catch(errorHandler))`. An error recovery handler can intercept errors at specific pipeline stages, returning fallback data to allow subsequent stages to continue or re-throwing to abort.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of async Promise chaining and error propagation.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why is compose right-to-left while pipe is left-to-right?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `compose(f, g)(x)` mirrors mathematical notation `f(g(x))` (right-to-left). `pipe(f, g)(x)` mirrors Unix pipeline streams `x | f | g` (left-to-right), which is significantly more intuitive for developers reading sequential data transformations.

realWorldUseCases.description: Koa pipelines compose asynchronous middlewares into an onion-layered Promise execution chain.

howToExplain.opening: An asynchronous pipeline sequentially chains synchronous and asynchronous functions together, passing the resolved output of each stage to the next.
keyPoints: Uses Promise.resolve(x) to normalize synchronous and asynchronous return values.
pipe executes left-to-right; compose executes right-to-left.
Error handling can be unified or handled per-stage.
Standard architecture for data ETL pipelines and server middleware.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Point-free asynchronous pipelines turn complex nested async logic into clean, readable linear flows.
analogies: A factory conveyor belt: raw materials enter step 1, get painted at step 2, and packaged at step 3.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using forEach instead of reduce for async pipelines.
commonMistakes.why: forEach cannot wait for promises between steps.
commonMistakes.correct: Use reduce with Promise chaining or an async for...of loop.

followUpDeepDive.question: What is the TC39 Pipeline Operator (|>) proposal?
followUpDeepDive.answer: The Stage 2 Pipeline Operator proposal introduces native syntax: `value |> fnA(%) |> await fnB(%)`, eliminating the need for userland pipe/compose functions.
